extracted.intended_audience: practitioners before the USPTO (attorneys/agents), OED staff, and attorneys involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Official final order approving an Affidavit of Resignation under 37 C.F.R. §11.27 and ordering exclusion on consent for practice before the USPTO in trademark and non-patent matters; describes required contents of such affidavits, statutory/regulatory authority, publication requirements, and consequences for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to approve affidavit and exclude
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, the USPTO Director has the authority to approve Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude Respondent on consent from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director's statutory/regulatory authority is the basis for approving affidavits of resignation and entering exclusions on consent; citations must be included in the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO professional conduct rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is a 'practitioner' pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.1 and is subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility, 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq., and the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnote: the Code of Professional Responsibility applies to conduct prior to May 3, 2013, while the Rules of Professional Conduct apply to conduct on or after May 3, 2013.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED investigation authority (37 C.F.R. § 11.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.22, the OED Director may open an investigation of allegations that a practitioner violated the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and/or USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order notes that the OED investigation 'delved into and obtained information' about multiple state bar proceedings and specific misconduct allegations; §11.22 is the regulatory basis for such investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation required acknowledgements (37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation acknowledges (1) consent is freely and voluntarily rendered and not under coercion or duress; (2) awareness that the OED Director opened an investigation pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.22 and the nature of that investigation; (3) awareness of OED's opinion regarding specific alleged violations; (4) that, if applying for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume certain facts and that the respondent could not have successfully defended himself; (5) that the respondent has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60 and the consequences of consenting to exclusion; and (6) consent to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in trademark and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits submitted for exclusion on consent should include these acknowledgements verbatim or substantively to satisfy §11.27(a); the Final Order expressly approves the Affidavit as complying with §11.27(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption upon reinstatement (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a respondent who submitted an Affidavit of Resignation applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that (a) the facts regarding the respondent in the OED file are true, and (b) the respondent could not have successfully defended himself against the allegations embodied in the OED Director's opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption is limited to the reinstatement determination and is a condition respondents acknowledge when consenting to exclusion under §11.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion on consent: scope and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be excluded on consent from practice before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters commencing on the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exclusion is limited to trademark and other non-patent matters (not patent practice), is effective as ordered, and may be undertaken without admission of the disciplinary rule violations alleged in the investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's electronic FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders approving affidavits of resignation/exclusions on consent are publicly posted in the OED Reading Room for transparency and public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice: publication and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Exclusion on Consent', which must state the respondent's voluntary affidavit submission, that an investigation was pending, the nature of the investigation, the OED Director's opinion regarding specific violated provisions, the reinstatement presumption, and the statutory/regulatory authority for the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order supplies model language which the Official Gazette notice should follow materially; required elements include identification of the practitioner, summary of allegations, citations to the specific CFR provisions alleged violated, and citation to statutory authority (35 U.S.C. and 37 C.F.R.).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) — disreputable or gross misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) (A practitioner shall not engage in disreputable or gross misconduct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited by OED as one of the provisions the respondent is of the opinion to have violated; used as a basis for disciplinary concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(3) — illegal conduct involving moral turpitude
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(3) (A practitioner shall not engage in illegal conduct involving moral turpitude).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as an alleged violation; conduct involving moral turpitude (e.g., misappropriation of client funds) implicates this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) (A practitioner shall not engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations such as issuing checks on insufficient funds or misappropriating funds are referenced as conduct falling under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) (A practitioner shall not engage in other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A catchall for misconduct that undermines fitness to practice; cited by the OED Director in the opinion of violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — neglect of a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) (A practitioner shall not neglect a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to perform competent legal services or to keep clients informed can trigger this provision, as alleged in the underlying state bar matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112 — preserve identity of funds and property of client
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112 (A practitioner shall preserve the identity of funds and property of client).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations of commingling, depositing personal funds into a client trust account, issuing checks for personal expenses, and misappropriating client funds are relevant to this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct that support exclusion (state bar findings)
rubrics_metrics.description: State Bar proceedings referenced include findings/stipulations that the respondent: repeatedly issued checks drawn on his client trust account with insufficient funds; deposited personal funds into client trust account and issued checks for personal expenses; misappropriated client funds; intentionally/recklessly/repeatedly failed to perform legal services competently; failed to keep a client reasonably informed; failed to comply with membership records address requirements; failed to respond promptly to reasonable client status inquiries; failed to maintain client funds balances properly; and failed to cooperate in a disciplinary investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete examples of alleged misconduct illustrate the types of behavior that the OED Director considered in recommending exclusion on consent; they map to the cited CFR provisions (moral turpitude, dishonesty, neglect, failure to preserve client funds, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent obligations after exclusion (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order states that the respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §11.58 governs practice after exclusion and related duties; §11.60 governs reinstatement proceedings and the consequences (including presumptions) that apply to applicants who previously submitted affidavits of resignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement that affidavit may be submitted while investigation pending
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice states that the practitioner 'voluntarily submitted his affidavit at a time when a disciplinary investigation was pending against him.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits of resignation may be submitted while an OED investigation is pending; the Final Order may still approve the affidavit and order exclusion on consent.
